# Brief

Wrenfold Joinery builds and fits kitchens from one workshop with 46 staff across two shifts.

## What we heard before the first call
- Rework costs about 263,480 a year across remakes and second visits.
- The owner set a budget of 73,000 for the new panel saw.
- Fixing the quote delays is worth 96,400 a year in orders that now go elsewhere.
- Last spring brought a write-off of 23,750 in scrapped doors.
- Anything over 5,000 needs the owner's signature.
- The margin on fitted kitchens is 22% this year.
- The maintenance contract is worth 41,200 a year.
- Our day rate of 1,450 was shared with the office before the call.

## Notes
- The edge banding machine jams on long runs.
- Laminate offcuts pile up beside the panel saw before collection.
- A pallet of oak fronts warped in the damp loading bay last winter.
- The previous supplier promised their nesting tool would halve offcut waste.
- Every quote waits on the panel saw schedule.
- The cutting list names each panel by cabinet and room.
- Sheets come from Ashby Sheet Supply; the office moved away from Kestrin Boards last year.
- Gideon Pryce inspects the extractor fittings for the council.
- The site skipper takes the delivery note at the door.
- Silver handles and a lantern pendant are the finish most homeowners ask for.
- The local market favours fresh white doors, and large orders go out by freight.
- The office keeps a contact sheet for every homeowner and a route for each van.
- Orders reach the office at orders@wrenfoldjoinery.example.
